instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: An ever-present at the centre of the meanest defence outside the top four; commanding in the air and a genuine international-standard centre-half.
Past his peak but still a top-class finisher and the leading scorer.
Three goals in 34 starts at Leeds. Not a barren run for a still-good striker; the finishing itself had gone.
Sixteen starts at Southampton at 29; two years on from his last rated season and no longer a first pick anywhere.
Marginalised under Kenny Dalglish and reduced to 20 starts.
PFA and FWA Player of the Year. Elite one-v-one dribbler and crosser; held short of 90 by how little he offered without the ball.
Thirty-three, fourteen starts and a peripheral figure at Villa; a five-point drop that is age and marginalisation together.
The Real Madrid season that made the role famous; the same footballer Chelsea bought a year later, so the same number.
The best defensive midfielder in the world in these years and the reason the position carries his name; positioning and interception at a level nobody else in the league approached.
The screen in front of a title-winning defence that conceded fifteen league goals; world class, a rung below Lampard (90) only because his contribution is the harder one to see.
Thirty-four and rotated; the reading of the game is intact, the legs are not.
The season Ferguson picked him against every good midfield in Europe; energy, positional sense and use of the ball all at their peak.
Ulcerative colitis ended his season in late November; seven starts, and already short of the engine that made 2009/10.
Eighteen, and already the quickest player in the division; the end product was some way behind the pace.
Six goals from midfield in a relegated side; the season that earned the Leeds move.
Thirty-five starts for a relegated City; his last full season before the knee gave way.
A broken ankle in January cost him half the season; before and after it he was already one of the best long passers in the league at 22.
His best Liverpool season and the one Real Madrid bought.
Twelve league goals and comfortably Fulham’s best attacker; the season the running and the finishing arrived together.
Seventeen league goals from wide and off the striker, a Fulham record for a Premier League season; his best year, and good enough to earn the move to Spurs.
On loan at 19 and clearly the most gifted crosser in a relegated side, without yet the consistency to be more than that.
His peak: thirty-seven starts, an England cap and the delivery that got him the Tottenham move.
Out of the side within eighteen months of the transfer, and the decline is real rather than tactical.
A difficult first English season spent adapting to the physical demands; the technique and movement that made him a 90 were already visible in seven assists.

Footballer of the Year, and the best player in the division until a cruciate rupture in March ended his season; nine goals and fifteen assists from 27 starts. Seven points up on his adaptation season, which is what the year merited.
Fourteen league goals from 21 starts in the season after a cruciate rupture; the pace never fully returned, the finishing and the timing more than covered for it.
World class that season — fourteen goals and eight assists from the left in an unbeaten side.
Thirty-one and a step slower in his last Arsenal season, but still creating at a level almost nobody in the league reached.
Half a season in a collapsing side, with his mind on a move that came in February (Anzhi); a little below his 2009–11 level.
Twelve league goals from 859 minutes, mostly from the bench. Rated on finishing ability, not on the limited starting role behind Yorke and Cole.
Seventeen league goals from 23 starts, his best return over a full season; finishing of a genuinely elite standard even while rotated.
Used wide and off the bench before the knee trouble that ended his career took hold; no league goals, but the fall is one of role and fitness rather than ability.
Back from two lost years at thirty-three; the finishing was untouched, the movement around it was not.
Twenty-one league goals, but eleven of them penalties, for a side that went down. Genuinely explosive pace and a sharp finisher; limited in the air and in link play, so good rather than elite.
Seven starts across an injury-wrecked season; the pace that was the whole of his game had started to go with the knee.
Fifteen starts before the move to Celtic in December; no drop in level, just half a season.
A World Cup winner months earlier and among the best defenders in the world; a shade below his Milan peak but still elite, above Adams (88) in 1998/99.
Thirty-four, fifteen starts, and losing the shirt to John Terry; the pace and the recovery were finally gone.
Thirty-six starts and Chelsea’s player of the year in a side that took a Champions League place on the last day; for two seasons among the best three or four keepers in the division.
Banned from late January after Selhurst Park. Rated on the football played, not the games missed.
Captain and champion again but visibly declining; retired at the end of the season aged 30.
Three starts at 30 after Derby’s relegation; effectively out of the top flight.
Four years on from the 1997/98 row: a raw teenager at Palace then, a functioning Premier League centre-forward by 23.
An ever-present in Reading’s seventh-placed first season and capped by England; the left foot did all of it.
An ever-present in the fifteen-point Sunderland side, which is evidence about the side rather than about him.
Five starts at 34; below the standard by then.
Chronic back and shin problems; effectively his last season of regular football, at 25.
Seventeen, thrown in at centre-half, and physically already a Premier League player.
Back to his best at right-back in City's title season, flying forward from defence and recalled by England, before Zabaleta took the shirt in the run-in.
On loan and central to the Great Escape; left foot, pace and a genuine top-flight athlete at nineteen.
A miserable season at Spurs with no league goals, but a forward who had scored heavily below and became a genuinely good Premier League centre-forward later. Rated between the two.
Two league goals in thirty-two starts, but the hold-up play and the link were the reason he started every week.
His best season: eight goals, a Europa League run led from the front, and an England call-up at twenty-nine.
A broken leg in September; nine starts, and five goals in them.
A rotation option in his first English season, but the technique, the left foot and the finishing were already exceptional. Rated as the twenty-one-year-old he was, not the player he became.
Only fourteen starts before the ankle injury on international duty, but nine goals and seven assists in them; when fit he was unambiguously Arsenal’s best player.
Eighteen goals in nineteen starts once the ankle healed — the best finisher in the league over the second half of the season, on a third of a campaign.
Thirty league goals, the Golden Boot and both Player of the Year awards in his first injury-free season; he carried Arsenal alone and was the best forward in the league.
Three starts at 39 as emergency third-choice cover; rated as the player he was at that point, not the Leeds keeper of 1992.
A record fee for a midfielder and an awkward first season positionally; the engine and the tackling were elite from the start.
Ten starts after a cruciate injury; the same player when fit, which is what the rating says.
A cruciate injury in pre-season kept him out until February, and the knees had taken the edge off the engine that made him elite.
Fourteen goals and genuinely frightening in a straight line; the finishing never caught up with the pace.
Nine starts after the Leeds move; could not get in the side.
Thirty-six starts for a relegated Norwich; still frightening in a straight line, still an unreliable finisher.
Germany’s first choice and an ever-present in an unbeaten side; elite, a rung below the very best keepers.
Ten clean sheets across a Champions League run at thirty-five; his best Arsenal season after the first.
Lost the shirt to Almunia and did not get it back.
